en.title: ioa in creioane (pencils)
en.summary: This item illustrates the Romanian triphthong ioa as found in the noun creioane.

sections.title: The group ioa
paragraphs: The group ioa makes the complex sound /jo̯a/. You hear it in the word (creioane) /kreˈjo̯a.ne/, which means pencils. This group makes only one sound in Romanian. It glides through three vowels in one breath.

sections.title: How to say ioa
paragraphs: Start with your tongue high and front, as in yes. Pull your lips into an open ring for an o vowel. Open your mouth wide right away to finish on a clear a. Your voice runs smoothly through all three positions without stopping. Place your hand on your throat to feel continuous vibration.

sections.title: Spelling rules for ioa
paragraphs: The letters ioa appear inside stressed syllables. They sound like /jo̯a/ in the word (aripioară) /a.riˈpjo̯a.rə/. The three letters always stay together in the same beat.

sections.title: Common mistakes with ioa
paragraphs: Do not split this group into separate syllables. English words rarely combine these three sounds in one push. Connect the glide directly into the vowel as in the start of yard, but pass quickly through an o. Keep your tongue active and avoid pausing between the vowels.
